This page is the hub for the org-wide standards that the other Contribute pages point to. Rather than repeat the rules everywhere, Contributing, Reporting issues & support, Security policy & reporting, and Releases & versioning all defer here for the shared conventions. Two pvarki repos define those conventions:

  • pvarki/markdown-pvarki-best_practises — documentation, Markdown, and dev-environment conventions.
  • pvarki/config-ci-library — the shared CI building blocks (reusable actions, pre-commit configs, image publishing).

markdown-pvarki-best_practises

The best-practises repo is the reference for how docs and developer environments are expected to look. The legacy docker-rasenmaeher-integration/README.rst links it directly from its Windows notes:

Use WSL, see best_practises repo for instructions on how to set it up.

Key points it covers (link out rather than duplicate here):

  • Markdown / documentation style — house conventions for the prose and code blocks in these repos.

  • Windows / dev-environment setup — use WSL, not git-bash, for the Docker-based legacy stack. Make sure your editor or git client does not rewrite line endings. For a CLI git client the README spells out the fix:

    git config --global core.eol lf
git config --global core.autocrlf false

config-ci-library

config-ci-library is the shared CI library every product repo pulls from, so checks stay consistent across the org. You will see it referenced as pvarki/config-ci-library/.github/actions/<name>@main and via its hosted pre-commit configs. From the integration-template scaffolding and the matrix-rmapi workflows, the pieces in active use include:

  • Reusable composite actions, e.g.

    • actions/setup-python and actions/setup-typescript — pinned toolchains for CI jobs.
    • actions/validate-bumpversion — enforces a version bump on every PR (see Releases & versioning).
    • actions/snyk-test (on PRs) and actions/snyk-monitor (on main) — dependency vulnerability scanning, org deployapp-products.
    • actions/publish-image — builds and pushes the product container image to the configured registries (GHCR / Docker Hub / ACR).

  • Shared pre-commit configs fetched during scaffolding. The integration template's copier.yml pulls a pinned config from config-ci-library and writes it to .pre-commit-config.yaml, choosing a python or python+typescript variant depending on the integration type:

    config-ci-library/pre-commit/configs/python.pre-commit-config.yaml
config-ci-library/pre-commit/configs/python+typescript.pre-commit-config.yaml

Running the checks locally

Across the repos the entry point is the same:

pre-commit install --install-hooks
pre-commit run --all-files

Parser-required linters (ruff, mypy, prettier, eslint) run against rendered output; the integration template wires these through nox (uvx --with nox nox -s lint).

Versioning conventions

The product repos increment versions with bump-my-version and CI verifies the bump on every PR via validate-bumpversion. The mechanics and release-notes formats are covered on Releases & versioning.
